mcqs.title: Labels and positions
mcqs.stem: A table has row labels [104, 101, 107, 103, 109], in that order. Which labels are selected by table.iloc[1:3]?
mcqs.rationale: iloc selects positions 1 and 2 and excludes position 3. The labels at those positions are 101 and 107.

mcqs.title: Combining conditions
mcqs.stem: Which mask selects movie records rated at least 8 AND with a production budget below 50,000,000?
mcqs.rationale: The required boundaries are >= 8 and < 50000000. Parentheses and & combine the two elementwise comparisons.

mcqs.title: Keeping a renamed result
mcqs.stem: A DataFrame named selected_movies contains 'gross_minus_budget_millions'. You run report = selected_movies.rename(columns={'gross_minus_budget_millions': 'gross_budget_gap_millions'}). Which statement is correct?

options.text: Both tables now use the new column name.
report is None because rename always changes the original table.
Neither table uses the new column name until the notebook is saved.
report uses the new column name, while selected_movies keeps the old name.

mcqs.rationale: rename returns a new DataFrame by default. Assigning its result keeps the renamed table without renaming the original.

mcqs.title: Choosing a denominator
mcqs.stem: A movie table has 100 records, of which 10 have missing ratings. Of the 90 records with observed ratings, 18 have ratings of at least 8. What proportion of records with observed ratings have a rating of at least 8?
mcqs.rationale: The question conditions on an observed rating, so the denominator is 90, not all 100 records.

rubric.evidence: 1 point: predictions and visible selection results; 1: correct label-versus-position explanation; 1: both shapes and Series-versus-DataFrame explanation.
1 point: movie import and original shape; 1: correct two-condition mask; 1: explicit copied subset with requested columns and row count; 1: ordered sorting, first five rows, and tie explanation.

1 point: correct rowwise difference in millions; 1: displayed results and units; 1: interpretation of negative values and limitation as a profit measure (0.5 each); 1: retained rename, both column-name outputs, and explanation of returned result.

1 point: observed-rating subgroup from the full original table; 1: numerator, denominator, guarded ratio; 1: missing-value and subgroup-denominator explanation; 1: median of the renamed gap variable interpreted for selected movies in millions of dollars.
0.5 point: name and readable, organized code, outputs, and explanations; 0.5: completion note describing fresh run, save, and HTML inspection. The HTML itself does not prove execution history.
